slot.brief: Draw the structure of a substituted cycloalkene or alkene (figure) and ask for the carbonyl fragment(s) obtained after ozonolysis with reductive workup.

stem: The alkene, as shown in the figure, undergoes ozonolysis followed by reductive workup with $\text{Zn}/\text{H}_2\text{O}$. The major product formed is:

verdicts.working: Figure shows 1-methylcyclohexene. Ozonolysis with Zn/H2O (reductive) cleaves C1=C2 without further oxidation: the fully substituted carbon (bearing CH3) gives a methyl ketone, the CH carbon gives an aldehyde. Ring opening yields CH3-CO-(CH2)4-CHO, a 7-carbon keto-aldehyde = 6-oxoheptanal, matching option B's structure. (A) would require unsubstituted cycloheptene; (C) requires 1,2-dimethylcyclopentene; (D) is the oxidative-workup product.

working:
1. The starting material is 1-methylcyclohexene.
2. In ozonolysis, the carbon-carbon double bond ($\text{C}=\text{C}$) is cleaved.
3. Under reductive conditions ($\text{Zn}/\text{H}_2\text{O}$), the cleavage proceeds without oxidation of aldehydes to carboxylic acids:
   - Carbon C1 has a methyl substituent and a ring carbon (disubstituted alkene carbon, no hydrogen attached). Upon cleavage, it forms a ketone carbonyl: $-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{CH}_3$.
   - Carbon C2 has one ring carbon and one hydrogen atom (monosubstituted alkene carbon). Upon cleavage, it forms an aldehyde carbonyl: $-\text{CH}=\text{O}$.
4. Opening the six-membered ring gives an acyclic 7-carbon chain:
$$\text{O}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{CH}_3$$
5. Numbering from the principal functional group (aldehyde carbon as C1):
- C1: $-\text{CHO}$
- C2 to C5: four $-\text{CH}_2-$ groups
- C6: $-\text{C}(=\text{O})-$
- C7: $-\text{CH}_3$

The IUPAC name of the product is 6-oxoheptanal.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A (heptanedial): Arises if the methyl substituent at C1 is overlooked, assuming both alkene carbons yield aldehydes (as with unsubstituted cyclohexene).
Option C (heptane-2,6-dione): Arises if both ends of the cleaved double bond are mistakenly assumed to become ketones.
Option D (6-oxoheptanoic acid): Arises from assuming oxidative workup (e.g. with $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$) instead of reductive workup, which would oxidize the aldehyde to a carboxylic acid.

figure.description: A skeletal structure of 1-methylcyclohexene: a six-membered ring (cyclohexene) oriented with a double bond between carbon-1 and carbon-2, and an exocyclic single bond from carbon-1 to a methyl group (labeled CH3). No other substituents or charges are present.
